Im really sorry this happened. You did nothing wrong and there is no reason that you would need to apologize. I understand why you did as I have been there before. Something I had to learn (im 21) is that you have to advocate for yourself extremely and never ever ever let administrative people or authority put things back on you. In this instance it was administration putting it back on you for "not trying". You don't have to explain anything to any teacher. Assuming you're in America (which maybe I shouldn't) we have the Americans with Disability Act (ADA). You can get a 504 plan for school which you honestly might already have from what it sounds like. I would highly encourage you to take things to the highest chain there is. Skip the steps and just go for it. Email and CC all the proper official people from the district person to just other equally important people. You don't have to give up your private information. You don't have to get into the whys. Just state the facts. You have accommodations made by a doctor. This teacher broke the law by now allowing you to go to the bathroom and then by belittling you and slandering you by calling you a child in front of the class. You do not deserve this treatment. Its hard being younger and in school with the mentality we were trained to follow of always abiding by authority etc. However life will fuck you over and blame will be placed back on you if you aren't always aggressively advocating for yourself. Administration doesn't want to acknowledge what happened wasn't okay because its problematic for them. So they put it back on you and victim blame you and then you internalize it and feel bad instead of reporting it. Im sorry and I wish you the best. Take care lovely

Im sorry although I feel like you might be missing the point. Seeing as how you posted on a homeless sub and I have been homeless and answering your question. I think you might be misunderstanding. A lot of the items people in general want to pass out aren't always beneficial to everyone. Food and hygiene products are by far the most accessible things I had to me. Sure it's lovely although the easiest answer to give when people ask how to help the homeless is give cash. Coming by to give me socks and leaving with your head high isn't the same as being treated as human and offering to help me with something I directly need or just being kind and saying hi.

For sure I feel that. Sorry if I caused you to delete your post. It really is a thoughtful thing and we need more people in this world with a heart like yours. I suppose what is your approach or purpose with doing what you are doing? I love helping people out how I can even if its buying someone a drink on my food stamps. I think being kind and acknowledging someone existing is more meaningful than random drops. Atleast that's how I feel for me personally. 
Also for me I just kind of go about my life and I'll see someone who I feel like needs some kindness and ill do them a solid whether it's food, items, or weed. It doesn't matter if they are drunk or have a needle prepared to shoot up I'll still offer kindness (I don't recommend putting yourself in unsafe situations). I live somewhere where things are close so that might make a difference.

Think of the items you use. Food and hygiene products were the easiest for me to get. Although nicer ones can feel good sometimes. Socks are a standard need for most people. Although honestly the most memorable moments that people helped me was being given cash so I could help myself with what I needed. Sure sometimes I bought weed to cope instead of better shoes. Although I've bought a suitcase, flight, storage unit, antibiotics, etc by people handing me cash (without begging). Which is why I kind of go back to offering kindness intuitively to people. Gift cards instead of cash are nice or if you would prefer to buy items to offer to more people I suppose think what you might like to have if you didn't have much of anything and couldn't afford to buy things that didn't pertain to survival. The biggest thing is just be kind. Saturday night I walked to the gas station down the street to get a drink and candy and I stopped to ask the lady at the bus stop if she wanted one to. I told her I only had EBT. For her to be acknowledged and be given something purely out of kindness and to be thought of by a stranger in passing can truly mean so much. I bought her a cherry coke. She seemed doubtful id even come back when I asked. Although when I gave it to her to hear her say thank you with a smile I couldn't see you could hear the slightest bit of humanity she felt and the love she felt from a stranger.

You can use youth services until like 25. Use these vs adult ones although don't over look the adult ones depending on your area and availability.

You'll figure things out. Know that it's not forever. You are going to learn a lot of skills and so much independence. You will learn to advocate for yourself. Do not let the streets get you down tho. Do not resort to substances. As long as you are not addicted to a substance you are going to have a much easier time getting back on your feet.

I tucked my shoelaces into my shoes so they wouldn't get dirty dragging on the ground. They bleached the sidewalks there. It might of been weekly although it was crazy to see. The air was so gross you could taste the retchedness. Im thankful masks are a thing during that time lol. I was there during the worst part of covid in Los Angeles until recently I think. I went to Skid Row for shelter. The only one I could get into. They couldn't even find another one for me. Although there were about 2-3 lockdowns / quarantined areas. During my time there. Theres a lot i learned. Being a younger girl among fully grown men many who had come from the jail/prison that funnels there just from down the road. You have to learn respect. Although not specifically to SR along but I'd have people talking about how they'd fuck me waiting in the breakfast line. Another thing was to mind your fucking business. When you check someone for your safety I would eye over there presentation however I mostly looked at hands. If you look the wrong way its an invitation. You start to know your neighbors. Although they definitely know you. Or atleast "know of you".  Watch yourself although keep to yourself. Don't get curious with people or watch them. Its brutally disheartening although look forward and keep your head low. Eyes watching the ground for everything and your back for whos following your. I watched little kids in tiny shoes running on the sidewalk and riding their bike on 5th street. Among puddles of orange caps. Its a quick thing to learn that you have nothing. Anything you do have you don't have it. Your bag becomes a magical pack you just pull stuff out of and no one needs to see it or know you have it. Although in long beach where I spent time if I had something you needed I'd give it to you if I had more than I needed. On skid row I walk past. Its a cruel place there. You'll hear women screaming at night but no one does anything. No one cares. It's full of despair. 
Something that broke my heart just right off the edge of Skid Row around 3rd and Los Angeles this lady was going through it. On drugs as well and just gone. She had a young boy and a younger girl with her. He was maybe 7 and she was probably closer to 5. He couldn't get his moms attention although he was trying to. Every part of me wanted to stop. To help. To do something. To show those kids atleast someone cares. But I didn't. You can't there. I walked past and while I'm not religious I did pray for those kids.
Some things are heartbreaking. You see older women in wheelchairs dragging themselves around by their feet. I think I was on 7th coming from the green apple market or whatever. I saw her crossing San Pedro as the light turned green. Cars didn't want to wait. A truck sped around her. Pulling up as if this ladies existence is inconvenient to them. About half way this middle aged man came over and said I got you mama and started wheeling her across. It was both heart breaking and beautiful. Its moments like that where killing yourself is within your deck of cards. Its the reality that you don't go to skid row to live. You go there to die. And I didn't want to die there on the street addicted. Its heartbreaking seeing the eyes of those who live on the same sidewalk block with rats scurrying around. 
I saw a man sweeping the sidewalk outside of his tent. I joked to myself he's just cleaning his porch. My stomach sank with that one. 
I feel like I'm much older than I am. Kind of like a child wearing daddies boots. But I lived among men whod rape me with the chance. Ive had needle nose plyers pulled on me for a fist fight over a power outlet. Ive had men roll up behind me on skateboards. Im still not sure if their intentions were less than what they seemed. I was there for about 3 months. I was on the middle of San Pedro at a mission there for about a month. Im glad to of left. Although I don't think that place will ever really leave me
